items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: he heard the best he knew, Papa C, he heard everybody here and at that time they were great trumpet players

ctx.x: what was the difference in their style?

Well, there's a big difference. one was lyrical which from, from a classical vein, technically musical because Bix was a, uh, was interested in concert music and Debussy and Ravel and his thing was semi-classical, that In the Mist and a couple of piano pieces he wrote which had a, a great significance of creative inventiveness but based from a European, a classical vein where Louis stuff was so black out of the Baptist Church and out of the honky tonks and, uh, out of, uh, a tradition of New Orleans trumpet…
